note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Minimal attribute-computation paths found by iterative patching show factual recall is multi-layer, non-contiguous and redundant

nodes.name: Retrieval is ill-defined
nodes.description: It is unclear whether factual retrieval is continuous accumulation across layers or a discrete state at which the entity representation can elicit the attribute, and the transformations the entity undergoes are largely unmapped.

nodes.name: Minimal attribute path defined
nodes.description: A minimal attribute computation path is a subset of layers applied to the entity representation that suffices for the model to produce the target attribute and in which no layer can be removed without hurting the computation.

nodes.name: Lock finds the endpoint
nodes.description: The lock operation (copying a layer's entity output to all higher layers) identifies the earliest layer l_attr after which no further computation on the entity tokens is needed.

nodes.name: Isolate with counterfactual patching
nodes.description: The isolate operation feeds the clean entity embedding only through candidate path layers and passes counterfactual activations through the remaining layers, so a layer is non-essential if the prediction survives its replacement.

nodes.name: Greedy search for minimal path
nodes.description: An iterative greedy search extends a path prefix by skipping as many layers as possible while remaining valid, yielding a minimal path; relaxing the upper bound to the last layer yields alternative minimal paths.

nodes.name: Attribute computation ends early-to-mid
nodes.description: On 2,000 CounterFact prompts, attribute computation completes in early-to-mid layers, with average l_attr of 4.61 (LLaMA 3.1 8B) and 7.97 (Qwen3 8B).

nodes.name: Paths are multi-layer and non-contiguous
nodes.description: Almost all paths contain more than two layers (mean length 5.91 LLaMA, 7.97 Qwen), and 33.1% (LLaMA) and 78.6% (Qwen) skip at least one layer, so no single layer retrieves a fact.

nodes.name: Alternative paths exist
nodes.description: Non-identical alternative functionally-equivalent paths exist in 80.1% (LLaMA) and 82.7% (Qwen) of cases.

nodes.name: Alternative paths are longer and deeper
nodes.description: Alternative paths are longer (mean 9.47 LLaMA, 10.47 Qwen), use bigger jumps (mean skip 6.46 and 10.4 layers) and end deeper (mean l_attr 13.93 and 18.06), while the primary path is the most compact route.

nodes.name: Hybrid paths succeed
nodes.description: Combining a primary-path prefix with an alternative-path suffix gives a working distinct path for 35.4% of LLaMA prompts and 32.8% of Qwen prompts, showing layer roles are not one-to-one across paths.

nodes.name: Representation at l_attr is necessary but often insufficient alone
nodes.description: Overwriting the l_attr representation with a counterfactual disrupts prediction in over 94% of cases, but injecting it alone into higher layers restores the attribute for only about 56% of LLaMA primary paths, so intermediate path layers are also needed.

nodes.name: Longer paths need inter-token propagation
nodes.description: Longer paths rely on inter-token transfer: 50.1% of LLaMA primary paths (avg length 7.4) and 80.6% of alternative paths need a propagating layer, versus shorter paths when not required; Qwen shows the same pattern.

nodes.name: Knowledge is distributed and redundant
nodes.description: Factual knowledge computation is distributed and redundant: no single layer or range is responsible for a given fact, and the same fact can be computed via multiple paths.

nodes.name: Explains localization-editing mismatch
nodes.description: Because attribute computation needs multiple transformations of the entity representation, editing succeeds by intervening at a necessary transformation stage rather than where the knowledge is localized, which may explain the localization-editing mismatch.

isolated_nodes.name: Entity resolution not a prerequisite
isolated_nodes.description: Explicit entity-resolution steps (Patchscopes decoding of the full name) are detected in only 12.9% (LLaMA) and 9.1% (Qwen) of primary paths, so detectable entity resolution is not a universal prerequisite for factual recall.

isolated_nodes.name: Roughly 15% need Layer 0 propagation
isolated_nodes.description: About 15% of all paths across both models require clean information propagation as early as Layer 0, which is unexpected under the paper's hypothesis.

isolated_nodes.name: Relation order shows no strong trend
isolated_nodes.description: No strong effect of placing the relation before or after the entity was found, beyond paths ending later in LLaMA.

isolated_nodes.name: Counterfactual noise has little effect
isolated_nodes.description: A noise-free variant of isolate leaves primary path lengths nearly unchanged (LLaMA 5.88 vs 5.91; Qwen 7.92 vs 7.97), though alternative paths terminate deeper.

isolated_nodes.name: Path length vs relation specificity is inconsistent
isolated_nodes.description: Broad relations (e.g., Continent) sometimes need fewer layers than specific ones (e.g., Headquarters), but the length ranking is highly inconsistent across models and between primary and alternative paths.

structural_reasoning: Method definitions lead to main empirical findings (early-mid completion, non-contiguity, redundancy) and then to the distributed-knowledge interpretation.
